title: Large Language Diffusion Models
notes: Source: arXiv:2502.09992v3 (18 Oct 2025), 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025); 33 pages (main text pp. 1-10, references pp. 10-18, Algorithms 1-5 and Appendix A pp. 19-22, Appendix B pp. 22-29, Appendix C p. 29, Tables 14-19 pp. 30-33). Authors: Shen Nie, Fengqi Zhu, Zebin You, Xiaolu Zhang, Jingyang Ou, Jun Hu, Jun Zhou, Yankai Lin, Ji-Rong Wen, Chongxuan Li (Renmin University of China; Ant Group). Project page and code (printed in the abstract): https://ml-gsai.github.io/LLaDA-demo/. Not printed in the PDF, added by the converter for convenience: the code repository is https://github.com/ML-GSAI/LLaDA and the checkpoints are GSAI-ML/LLaDA-8B-Base and GSAI-ML/LLaDA-8B-Instruct on Hugging Face.

Mathematics is transcribed to LaTeX from the authors' arXiv TeX source (macros from math_commands.tex expanded) and checked against the PDF; equation numbers are \tag{1}-\tag{16}; the n-turn dialogue split in B.1 is unnumbered as printed. No disagreement between TeX and PDF was found. The mask token is written $\mathrm{M}$, the indicator $\mathbf{1}[\cdot]$, the end-of-sequence token as $|\text{EOS}|$ in the main text and as plain |EOS| in Appendix B (both render the same).

The authors' slips are kept as printed, not corrected: 'remarked' for 'remasked' (Sec. 2.4); Eq. (13) subscript $p_{\text{data}(x_0)}$; Algorithm 2 comment truncated to 'the SFT dat'; Algorithm 3 reuses $i$ as loop and sum index; 'Block Difusion' (Tables 7 and 8); Table 9 header 'Length' over the strategy rows; 'baelines' (Table 19 caption); 'just one tokens are transferred' (B.5); 'Tab. 11 compares of memory consumption' (B.7); '31th' in references [101]-[102]; in the iGSM prompt (B.8) the TeX accent artefacts '¨the number' and 'High.Ässume'. Model outputs quoted in Tables 15 and 17 keep their own errors ('immaginiert'; GPT-4o's '山居秋膜', '无亲'). Note that the iGSM solution line '3 * 2 = 1' is arithmetic modulo 5, as the prompt states. Converter's observation (not a correction of the text): Algorithm 5 defines $n_{un} = \lfloor L(1-s) \rfloor$ as the number of unmasked tokens at time $s$ (line 12) but remasks the positions in '$\text{Lowest} - n_{un}$', commented as 'the $n_{un}$ positions with the least confidence'; the notation is not defined in the paper, and read literally this remasks $n_{un}$ instead of $L - n_{un}$ tokens. Section 2.4 (remask $\frac{s}{t}$ of the predicted tokens, i.e. about $Ls$ masked tokens at time $s$) and the released code (generate.py unmasks the most confident tokens, a fixed number per step) agree with $L - n_{un}$ remasked tokens.

Algorithms 1-5 (printed on pp. 19-21: Algorithms 1-3 above the Appendix A heading, Algorithms 4-5 within A.1) are placed at the end of A.3 'Algorithms', the section that presents them; each is an image crop followed by a line-by-line transcription (nesting shown by indentation). Other floats are placed at paragraph boundaries in the section that discusses them, which can differ from the printed position: Figure 2 after the opening paragraph of Section 2; Figure 3 inside 3.1 after 'Fig. 3 shows ...'; Table 3 in 3.4 Case Studies; Table 5 in B.2 after the sentence citing it and Tables 18-19 (Fig. 3 data, printed on the last page) after the 6ND paragraph of B.2; Table 6 at the end of B.3; Figure 4 after 'Flexible Sampling Strategies' in B.4; Tables 7-9 after the B.4 'Results' paragraphs; Table 10 in B.5; Figure 5 and Table 11 in B.7; Table 12 at the end of B.8; Tables 13-17 (case studies; Table 13 printed at the top of p. 29 before B.9, Tables 14-17 after Appendix C) in B.10.

Tables: cells are strings exactly as printed, shot counts kept in the cell (e.g. '65.9 (5)'), '-' for unknown values, footnote markers ∗ † ¶ kept in the model names; the header-type rows of Tables 1-2 (Model, Training tokens, Post-training, Alignment pairs) and the group rows (General Tasks, Mathematics & Science, Code, Chinese) are ordinary rows; Table 7 has added columns 'Strategy' and "L'" (the printed group label repeated on each row); Table 11 repeats the merged 'Input Length' cell on each row; Tables 15-17 (dialogue cases) are stored with a converter-added header 'Case | Speaker | Text', one row per printed turn, the case label repeated on each row of its case; where the printed table repeats a label for separate cases (separated only by horizontal rules) the converter numbers them: 'Daily life (1)', 'Daily life (2)', 'Translation (1)', 'Translation (2)' in Table 15 and 'Daily life (1)' (2 rounds), 'Daily life (2)' (4 rounds) in Table 16. Printed line breaks inside a cell are kept as \n (shown as
in the Markdown copy); the asterisks in Table 15's movie answer ('**The Shawshank Redemption**') are literal characters of the model output, which a Markdown renderer shows as bold. Bold best values (in all tables) and the vertical rules of Tables 1-2 are not carried into the CSVs; see the PDF.

Tables 3, 13 and 14 contain token visualisations (shading = order of prediction during sampling); each is kept as an image-only table (JPEG in assets/table/) with its caption, followed by a text transcription of the dialogue and of the token sequence read from the image. The shading exists only in the image. Figure 4's printed panel labels '(a) ... (b) ... (c) ...' precede its caption as a separate line.
source_review_notes: All 33 pages reviewed against page renders by three reviewer agents (pages 1-9, 10-22, 23-33; reports in reports/review-pages-*.md): equations (1)-(16) transcribed from the authors' TeX and compared with high-resolution crops; Algorithms 1-5 cropped and transcribed line by line; Figures 1-5 boxed as single crops with edges checked; Tables 1-2, 4-12, 15-19 transcribed cell by cell (Tables 18-19 also compared programmatically with the PDF text layer and the TeX); Tables 3, 13, 14 kept as images with transcriptions; 125 references checked in order against the bibliography. Remaining verifier diagnostics are LaTeX-notation differences (maths, U+2212 minus, powers of ten, equation tags), numbers repeated in transcriptions or merged cells, and glued table cells in the second parser, adjudicated per page.

navigation.heading: 2.2 Pre-training
navigation.purpose: Transformer without causal mask, 1B/8B variants, vanilla MHA (no KV cache), 2.3T tokens, 4096 length, 0.13M H800 GPU hours, 1% random-length data, Warmup-Stable-Decay schedule (4e-4 -> 1e-4 -> 1e-5), AdamW wd 0.1, batch 1280
